1.text: White throws near the bar, plays a checker, and picks up before the cube discussion. The pale dice overlap the point and rail in the footage.
Black moves 9/3 and 6/1. The two verified positions require 6–5. One die was misread as four by the detector.

3.text: White throws after the discussion and plays from the bar. The left die reads two. The other sits against the bar.
White throws and picks up a crowded pair on the lower left point. The dice were missed during the turn.
White throws and later picks up both dice by the left rail. A three remains visible across the settled frames.

4.text: White rolls and moves checkers between Black’s two indexed rolls. The left die shows six before the pickup.
Black’s 5–4 sits in the same two places through both of the earlier replay’s tick marks and through checker movement. Black collects the pair shortly before 5:12.
Black rolls onto a crowded point, immediately picks up, and leaves the black checker on the bar. Only one face is legible.
Black’s short roll lands among the lower-right checkers. Black immediately picks up, leaving the checker on the bar. White then throws from the left.
White picks up the 3–2 and makes the next visible throw. No Black throw occurs between these two pickups and throws in the recorded footage.

Black throws the 3–2 once and leaves both dice on the left through several checker rearrangements. The replay now scores the play from the board before the throw to the board after pickup. It drops the earlier 0.015 charge for an intermediate arrangement.

5.text: Both players pick up their individual opening dice and toss again. White’s six and Black’s five decide the opening. White plays 24/13. The sixth checker on point 13 obscured the completed board for the detector.
White moves two checkers from point 13 to point 1 and hits Black. Only double six legally produces the two verified boards. The detector had read one of the dice as five.
White throws as Black clears the last die. White’s bar/20 and 6/2 play resolves the pale pair as 5–4, including the face the detector read inconsistently.
White plays 14/9 and 6/5 before picking up. The two checker positions establish 5–1. A six from the detector is incompatible with the move.
